items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bill Russo’s arranger-copyist – Bill wanted us to play in Chicago. We said we had no music. Russo talked with him. They said this man that works for Bill Russo will listen to the recording and write it all down.

ctx.x: About you meeting Jimmy Lyons. You said he came and heard you at the Geary Cellar and at the Marines Memorial.

There he decided to have us do a show, and eight people were too many for NBC, but they would do it as a trio. That’s where I think Jimmy Lyons and I started getting more friendly and knowing each other. I’d appear a lot on his show. In fact if you’ve got the old octet record, Jimmy Lyons is narrating How High the Moon. So you know that he was involved. Then the classical – Maria Corbin was very impressed with the writing of the octet, considering it classical. So we right away were crossing between the jazz and…
This was for the Chicago Jazz Festival. Neil Tesser was the one. Do you know Neil? The writer.
